claims.claim_text: The probable Malcolm A. Crusius identity was an Assistant United States Attorney in New York in 1937; this is documented prewar work, not a demonstrated immediate pre-OSS affiliation.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Malcolm A. Crusius, Asst. U. S. Atty., of New York City, of counsel
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary federal appellate opinion names Malcolm A. Crusius as an Assistant U.S. Attorney; an official Army row records the same rare name with a lawyer/judge occupation code, and a 1945 Judge Advocate journal names a captain of that exact name.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable: exact uncommon name and middle initial plus concordant legal occupation and wartime Judge Advocate service, but no direct Box 157 or OSS-personnel identifier bridge.
claims.temporal_assessment: The 1937 federal role is definitely prewar and pre-OSS, but a multi-year gap prevents an immediacy claim.
claims.match_notes: The separate 1945 Army assignment is published only as temporally uncertain context. Box 157 must establish the OSS sequence.
